frequency_question: How often do U.S. administrations implement primary-tier secondary sanctions on major foreign banks within a single presidential term?
membership_rule: Includes executive branch actions targeting Tier-1 or systemically important foreign commercial banks with explicit secondary sanctions disconnecting them from the U.S. financial system for violating energy/oil sanctions regimes. Excludes mere warnings, minor non-bank entities, or tertiary financial institutions.

cases.name: Russia-related secondary sanctions framework targeting major foreign financial institutions

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 major structural enforcement cycles observed in modern secondary sanction history.
known_gaps: Limited to modern eras where primary-power financial dominance permitted extraterritorial enforcement of this scale.
skeleton: Two major sanctions enforcement cycles (Iran primary era 2012-2015, Russia primary/secondary financial enforcement era 2022-2026) featuring direct targeting mechanisms against systemically critical foreign banks.
multiplier: 2 cycles evaluated, major actions taken in both cycles = 2/2 baseline implementation frequency for major-power escalations.
validity_reason: Tied to the stability of the U.S. dollar hegemony and current statutory secondary sanctions authorities, which remain active through the current presidential term.
